item.description: Crown-of-thorns starfish are notorious for devouring coral reefs, but surprising new research reveals these spiny predators may actually help reefs thrive when their populations are kept in check. Scientists studying Australia's Great Barrier Reef discovered that nearly 75% of observed starfish feeding events left behind living coral tissue, rather than destroying entire colonies. By feeding on fast-growing, dominant corals, the starfish create opportunities for slower-growing species to survive, potentially increasing coral biodiversity. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.description: In a heartfelt farewell, a Melbourne couple bid adieu to their beloved Maidstone home, a cherished sanctuary for over four decades after immigrating from Lebanon in 1982. Reassured by the buyers' intention to cherish the house rather than demolish it, the couple found solace in their memories. This sale marks a poignant shift as they prepare to embrace a new chapter in Taylors Lakes. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro posts video, says he fled Brazil due to ‘persecution’
item.description: Brazil's defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro posted a video message on social media late Friday to declare he had fled to the US because he was a victim of 'persecution'.
